author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it by full name, on one unpaginated page, reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's specialties, when GET /specialties.html is requested, then every specialty is listed by its stored name on a single page with no pagination
given a veterinarian holding a specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian is listed under it by first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary")
given a veterinarian holding several specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian is listed under each of them
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears nowhere on the page
edge case 1: a specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian under it
edge case 2: specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are presented in a stable order

the page carries the existing site navigation (REQ-SYS-001) and all its fixed wording is translated in every supported language (REQ-LANG-002); stored specialty names and veterinarian names are data, not wording
non_goals: managing veterinarians or specialties (NG-2, unchanged per owner decision)
a navigation entry or any link to the page from another page (owner: "A visible entry point may come as a follow-up request.")
listing veterinarians who hold no specialty
notes: Address GET /specialties.html is owner-stated (intake line 1). No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. No prd-autofix records to audit. Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions, taken at the narrowest reading per the owner's instruction: (1) visible entry point deferred; (2) specific ordering unstated, only a stable order required; (3) presentation of a specialty held by no vet unstated, listed with no vet under it and no 'none' wording required. A design is free to choose any stable order; tests should pin the chosen one.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The page fits the vet feature package (system-design § Package Structure, § Contracts) using patterns already in force: a lookup-value repository on the PetTypeRepository precedent, a web controller route next to /vets.html, and a Thymeleaf template under templates/vets. The adjustment: a specialty no veterinarian holds must still be listed, so Vet records alone are not enough. A new uncached SpecialtyRepository reads all specialties. A new immutable value object, SpecialtyDirectory, holds every directory rule (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog: Value object; the Web controller row admits no business rule): grouping by specialty identity, omitting veterinarians with no specialty, and the stable order (specialties by name then id; veterinarians by last name, first name, then id; each shown as 'first last'). VetController reads both repositories, constructs the directory, and returns the view. It contains no grouping or sorting. Design-doc writes: REQ-VET-003 added to the Contracts rows for Vet, Specialty, VetRepository, and VetController; new rows for SpecialtyRepository and SpecialtyDirectory; an invariant note; a new § Scale and Load section with this path's row; a provenance clause. Basis: grep and reading of VetController, VetRepository, Vet, Specialty, PetTypeRepository, and VetControllerTests (the IDE oracle is not connected, so this is the weaker basis). No ADR: there is no trade-off beyond this slice, and the pattern is already in the in-force catalog.
integration_points: Entry point GET /specialties.html in VetController binds no request input: no @RequestParam, no @ModelAttribute, and no persisted type is bound. The model carries only the SpecialtyDirectory. It is HTML only, with no serialized variant (REQ-VET-002 is withdrawn).

Repository boundary, SpecialtyDirectory tests: none. They build the directory from real Vet and Specialty instances (testing-principles § Mocking Policy: domain objects use real implementations). Directory rules and the PRD edge cases are pinned here.

Repository boundary, VetControllerTests: SpecialtyRepository uses a hand-written in-memory double registered through a nested @TestConfiguration (testing-principles § Mocking Policy: hand-write mocks). The VetRepository @MockitoBean stub stays, since the brief tolerates existing framework stubs; new tests reuse its findAll() setup and add no new stub kinds.
Framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned web-layer harness (CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy).

Template: uses the shared layout fragment like vets/vetList.html, so it carries the site navigation (REQ-SYS-001). No navigation entry is added (PRD non-goal). Every fixed string goes through a message key present in all eleven bundles; I18nPropertiesSyncTest enforces REQ-LANG-002. Specialty and veterinarian names render through escaped th:text, never th:utext.

patterns.description: Lookup-value repository shape for SpecialtyRepository: read-only, one find-all method
Route and view-name shape for the new GET handler
Layout fragment, table markup, and message-key use for the new template

risks.risk: Vets come from the cached VetRepository.findAll(), and specialties come from a separate uncached read. Their Specialty instances are different objects, and Specialty does not override equals.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory matches by Specialty id, never by reference or entity equals (system-design § Contracts invariant note). A test builds the vet's Specialty and the listed Specialty as distinct instances that share an id.

risks.risk: Specialty directory path scales with the specialty and veterinarian counts (system-design § Scale and Load, specialty directory row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: one pass grouping by specialty id into a map, then sorting each list with a standard Comparator. No pagination, no per-specialty query (avoids N+1).

risks.risk: A cached veterinarian could reference a specialty id missing from the fresh specialty read (system-design § Open Questions 5, vet cache invalidation).
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory ignores a held specialty absent from the specialty list rather than failing. The page lists only stored specialties (architecture-principles § Domain Core: errors flow outward; no exception is needed for a dropped reference).

risks.risk: Name ties make the order unstable (PRD edge case 2).
risks.mitigation: Identity is the final tie-breaker on both orders (system-design § Contracts invariant note); a test pins the order with tied names.

risks.risk: Placing the grouping in the controller would breach the Web controller row (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog).
risks.mitigation: All grouping, omission, and ordering live in SpecialtyDirectory; the controller test asserts only the view name and the model attribute.

notes: No design-doc-autofix records to audit. Open PRD questions are taken at the narrowest reading: the order is the one above, and a specialty held by no vet renders with an empty list and no 'none' wording. SpecialtyDirectory is a Java record with defensive copies (architecture-principles § Domain Core). It is not covered by the persistence-entity exception. Expose display-ready values (specialty name; vet full name 'first last'), not entities, so the template carries no logic.
